note:
Fork doc-payload classification (V2-506). Every file under docs/ (and the root HARNESS-V2-* program docs) is one of: 'fork' — a fork operating this template INHERITS it (ADRs, runbooks, recipes, rubrics, ledgers, the operational reference); or 'template-dev' — the TEMPLATE's own development history that a fork does not need. `npm run rebrand -- --prune-docs` reads this to print the prune list. Rules are FIRST-MATCH-WINS, top to bottom; the final catch-all defaults to 'fork' so an unclassified doc is KEPT (the safe failure).

UPDATED 2026-07-25 — the old note said template-dev docs are 'MOVED to an archive branch reference, NEVER deleted from template main'. That policy is SUPERSEDED: on 2026-07-25 the template-dev docs were REMOVED from main and pinned at the git tag `template-history-2026-07` (see docs/ARCHIVE.md). Reason: they were 65% of 3.23 MB of docs against 16k lines of product, and every session in this repo paid context tax on a closed program's build record. Git retains them at the tag; forks were never affected (they already pruned them). This manifest still classifies what remains, and still governs fork pruning. Two template-dev paths were deliberately KEPT in the tree: docs/verification/** (evidence backing live findings-register entries — deleting it would create dead evidence pointers) and docs/SESSION-HANDOFF.md + docs/session-state.json (live session state the SessionStart hook reads).

UPDATED 2026-07-25 (template-cleanliness audit) — both of those carve-outs were revisited, and the prune stopped being advisory:
(1) docs/verification/** is now SPLIT in practice, not by rule. The five sets photographing the removed Asset-Tracker demo domain went to the archive with the domain itself (they documented screens that no longer exist, so they were dead evidence either way); the sets documenting surviving surfaces — design-system/, v2-305-copy/, atomic-audit-triggers/ — stayed in the tree, and the two harness citations of a 'worked example' (.claude/rules/design.md, .claude/skills/design-qa/SKILL.md) were re-pointed at design-system/. The classification below still reads template-dev for the whole path, which is correct FOR A FORK: a fork inherits none of this template's evidence.
(2) docs/SESSION-HANDOFF.md + docs/session-state.json were REMOVED from main. The 'live session state' rationale holds on a working BRANCH, not on main — .claude/rules/harness.md says branch-only, never merged to main, and they had leaked there, so every fork started life carrying this template's harness-v2 program status. Nothing breaks when they are absent: .claude/hooks/session-start.sh writes a fresh valid skeleton (V2-006). scripts/ship.mjs now has a `session-state` gate that goes RED if either path is tracked while on main, so the leak cannot silently recur.
(3) `npm run rebrand -- --prune-docs` gained `--apply`, and a normal rebrand now runs it automatically (scripts/deploy.mjs shells out to it too). Before this, the prune was a list-only mode that no fork-creation path invoked — so every fork inherited the full template-dev payload regardless of this manifest.

rules.why: harness-v2 program artifacts (backlog/evidence/closeout) — the template's own build record

in-flight session state — GITIGNORED since 2026-07-25 (local to the machine, never committed anywhere). The rule still classifies it so the on-disk prune sweeps the regenerated file out of a fork's tree; it can no longer reach any branch.

per-session in-flight state (the SESSION-HANDOFF.md data source) — GITIGNORED since 2026-07-25 after leaking to main three times; local-only, regenerated as a skeleton at SessionStart (V2-006). The schema (session-state.schema.json) stays fork-inherited: a fork regenerates its own state against it.

WORKED EXAMPLE — cited by .claude/rules/design.md ('see docs/verification/design-system/ for the worked example') and .claude/skills/design-qa/SKILL.md. Those two files are fork-inherited and NOT covered by this manifest (it only classifies docs/**), so pruning this path would break the citation in every fork at the moment of fork creation — /rebrand now runs the prune automatically. First-match-wins: this must stay ABOVE the docs/verification/** catch-all.
WORKED EXAMPLE — holds the repo's only baseline/ directory, cited by .claude/skills/design-qa/SKILL.md as the visual-regression baseline example. Same fork-citation reasoning as design-system/.
LIVE EVIDENCE — backs the open SECURITY.md §16 atomic-audit row and an adjudicated findings-register entry; the trigger battery is the runnable artifact a fork applies. Not template build history.
design-QA evidence for the template's own build (the pattern is inherited via the recipes/rubric, not the evidence)
feature blueprints for capabilities the fork inherits (openapi seam, docs-site, egress bridge, style-guide, README)
ADRs — the architectural decision record the fork operates under (incl. ADR-TEMPLATE)
operational + maintainer runbooks the fork inherits
seed parity matrices for the benchmark loop
catch-all: operational reference (REPO-MAP, recipes, rubrics, ledgers, agent-memory, oss-catalog, ARCHITECTURE, mcp, session-state, manifests) — default KEEP is the safe failure
